entities.summary:
Dušan Samo Jurkovič was a Slovak architect, furniture designer, artist and ethnographer. One of the best-known promoters of Slovak art in 20th century Czechoslovakia, he is remembered mostly due to his projects of numerous World War I cemeteries in Galicia and thanks to his wooden works of spa complex in Luhačovice and mountain cottage hotel Maměnka and canteen Libušín in Pustevny.

Thanks to his artistic work with wood, he is referred to as "the poet of timber". His architectonic style was a unique fusion of folk architecture and then-popular architectonic styles, mostly associated with Art Nouveau. Dušan Jurkovič was a architects & engineers from Turá Lúka (1868-08-23, Turá Lúka–1947-12-21). A moderately significant entity in the historical record. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a prominent architect and furniture designer in early 20th century Czechoslovakia, Dušan Jurkovič's work had regional significance through his designs of World War I cemeteries and spa complexes, earning him the nickname 'the poet of timber'. His unique architectural style blended folk and Art Nouveau elements.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Dušan Jurkovič's architectural style blended folk and Art Nouveau elements, influencing Czechoslovakia's design landscape. His work on World War I cemeteries in Galicia had a lasting impact on memorial architecture.
